# Decode XORed Array.

@example 2 XOR 7 = 5 and 7 XOR 4 = 3, so arr = [2,7,4] gives this encoded list.
[5,3]
2
=> [2,7,4]

@example An XOR of 0 means a value equals the one before it, so all four are 9.
[0,0,0]
9
=> [9,9,9,9]

@example Each value is the one before it XOR the next entry: 6 ^ 12 = 10, 10 ^ 10 = 0, 0 ^ 15 = 15, 15 ^ 1 = 14.
[12,10,15,1]
6
=> [6,10,0,15,14]

# The shortest input: two values.
[0]
0
=> [0,0]

[100000]
100000
=> [100000,0]

# first at its largest, and nothing changes after it.
[0,0,0,0,0]
100000
=> [100000,100000,100000,100000,100000,100000]

# Each value builds on the one before it, not on first: XORing first with
# each entry would give [0,1,2,4,8].
[1,2,4,8]
0
=> [0,1,3,7,15]

# XOR is not addition: bits set in both numbers cancel.
[3,3,6]
1
=> [1,2,1,7]

# The same entry twice gets back to where it started.
[100000,100000]
0
=> [0,100000,0]

# A value above both 10^5 and 2^16 - 1: 65536 XOR 65535 = 131071.
[65535]
65536
=> [65536,131071]

# A chain that climbs above 10^5 and comes back down.
[31071,65535,1,100000,34463]
100000
=> [100000,131071,65536,65537,34465,62]
